transcript:
INTERVIEWER: Tell me about a time you owned a problem.
CANDIDATE: Our deploy step was flaky, so I took it on. I measured the failure rate at about 18%, traced it to a race condition in the migration script, and fixed it. After my change the failure rate dropped under 2%.
INTERVIEWER: How did you handle disagreement with a teammate on the approach?
CANDIDATE: A teammate wanted to just add retries. I disagreed but we talked it through, I showed the logs, and we agreed retries hid the bug. We went with the real fix and I owned the rollout.

INTERVIEWER: Tell me about an impactful project.
CANDIDATE: We built a new service and it went well. We shipped it and people liked it.
INTERVIEWER: What did you personally do, and what was the result?
CANDIDATE: I mean, we all worked on it. It was a team thing. I'm not sure about exact numbers, it just felt successful.

CANDIDATE: Before I code, let me restate the problem and think about complexity. A brute force is O(n^2); I can do O(n) with a hash map keyed on the complement. Let me write that.
CANDIDATE: I'll add a test for the empty array and for duplicates before I call it done.
INTERVIEWER: What if the input is sorted?
CANDIDATE: Good point — then a two-pointer is O(1) space, I'd switch to that.

CANDIDATE: Um, I'll just start coding. [long silence] ... this loop isn't working. Maybe another loop.
INTERVIEWER: What's the time complexity of your approach?
CANDIDATE: I'm not sure. I'll just try things until the example passes.
INTERVIEWER: Could a hash map help here?
CANDIDATE: Maybe? I'll keep using nested loops though.

INTERVIEWER: Why this role and why now?
CANDIDATE: I've wanted to work on infrastructure since my first internship where I got pulled into an on-call incident — debugging that system is what made me fall in love with backend reliability.
INTERVIEWER: What's a weakness you're working on?
CANDIDATE: I tend to over-engineer early. I've been practicing shipping a simple version first, then iterating.
INTERVIEWER: What do you know about our team?
CANDIDATE: Honestly not a lot of specifics, just that you do platform work.

CANDIDATE: First the user: I'd segment by new vs power users, and I think the sharpest pain is new-user activation. For a v1 I'd prioritize a guided first session by impact-vs-effort.
INTERVIEWER: How would you measure success?
CANDIDATE: Primary metric is day-7 retention, but I'd set a guardrail on support tickets and a counter-metric on notification opt-outs so we don't juice retention by spamming.
INTERVIEWER: If retention rises but engagement per session falls?
CANDIDATE: Then I'd dig in — retention from habit is good, but falling session depth could mean we front-loaded value; I'd look at the cohort curves before declaring a win.
